R Loading Process

  • Changed column names
  • Changed data types
  • Stored as a R Data Save (.rds)
load_salary_data.r 
library(tidyverse)
library(this.path)

df_fact <- read_csv(file.path(
  dirname(this.path()),
  "..",
  "data",
  "filtered_download",
  "pay_by_name_columns_and_hire_date.csv"
))

df_dim <- read_csv(file.path(
  dirname(this.path()),
  "..",
  "data",
  "filtered_download",
  "job_city_zip_agency_department_by_name_columns_and_hire_date.csv"
))

rows_prior <- nrow(df_dim)
df_dim <- df_dim %>%
  distinct(`First Name`,
           `Middle Initial`,
           `Last Name`,
           `Name Suffix`,
           `Orig Hire`,
           `Pyrl Fiscal Yr`,
           .keep_all = TRUE)
rows_after <- nrow(df_dim)
print(paste("Removed", rows_prior - rows_after, "rows to account for 
             employees with multiple parameters for the same year."))

df <- df_fact %>%
  left_join(df_dim, by = c(
    "First Name",
    "Middle Initial",
    "Last Name",
    "Name Suffix",
    "Orig Hire",
    "Pyrl Fiscal Yr"
  ))

df <- df %>%
  group_by(
    `First Name`,
    `Middle Initial`,
    `Last Name`,
    `Name Suffix`,
    `Orig Hire`
  ) %>%
  mutate(employee_id = cur_group_id()) %>%
  ungroup()

df <- df %>%
  select(
    -`Middle Initial`,
    -`Name Suffix`
  )

df <- df %>%
  rename(
    year = "Pyrl Fiscal Yr",
    first_name = "First Name",
    last_name = "Last Name",
    gross_pay = "Tot Gross",
    overtime = "Overtime",
    salary = "Salaries & Wages",
    hire_date = "Orig Hire",
    job = "Job Cd Descr",
    city = "City",
    zip = "Postal",
    # union = "Union Descr",
    agency = "Agency",
    department = "Department"
  )

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    first_name = as.character(first_name),
    last_name = as.character(last_name),
    gross_pay = as.numeric(gross_pay),
    overtime = as.numeric(overtime),
    salary = as.numeric(salary),
    hire_date = as.Date(hire_date, format = "%m/%d/%Y %I:%M:%S %p"),
    job = as.factor(job),
    city = as.factor(city),
    zip = as.factor(zip),
    agency = as.factor(agency),
    department = as.factor(department)
  )

saveRDS(df, file.path(
  dirname(this.path()),
  "..",
  "data",
  "clean",
  "annual_salary_data.rds"
))

R Cleaning Process

  • Remove rows with negative overtime, salary, and gross pay
  • Remove rows for individuals hired in 1900
  • Adjust hire date for individuals with a hire date after their first pay year
  • Account for Capitalized City Names
  • Remove Zipcode Extension
  • Added Name Column
clean_salary_data.r 
library(tidyverse)
library(this.path)


df <- readRDS(file.path(
  dirname(this.path()),
  "..",
  "data",
  "clean",
  "annual_salary_data.rds"
))


### Remove rows with undisclosed first and last name
rows_to_drop <- df %>%
  filter(first_name == "Undisclosed", last_name == "Undisclosed") %>%
  nrow()
df <- df %>%
  filter(first_name != "Undisclosed", last_name != "Undisclosed")
print(paste("Dropped", rows_to_drop, "due undisclosed name."))


### Remove rows with negative overtime, salary, and gross 
rows_to_drop <- df %>%
  filter(overtime < 0 | salary < 0 | gross_pay < 0) %>%
  nrow()
df <- df %>%
  filter(overtime >= 0, salary >= 0, gross_pay >= 0)
print(paste("Dropped", rows_to_drop, "due to negative pay."))

### Remove rows for individuals hired in 1900
rows_to_drop <- df %>%
  filter(hire_date == "1901-01-01") %>%
  nrow()
df <- df %>%
  filter(hire_date != "1901-01-01")
print(paste("Dropped", rows_to_drop, "due to invalid hire date. 
Note many are likely due to a join based on hire date."))

### Adjust hire date for individuals with a hire date after their first pay year
df <- df %>%
  group_by(employee_id) %>%
  mutate(first_year = min(year)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    hire_date = if_else(
      as.numeric(difftime(as.Date(paste0(year, "-07-01")), hire_date, "days")) < 0,
      as.Date(paste0(first_year, "-01-01")),
      hire_date
    ),
    years_since_hired = time_length(
      interval(hire_date, as.Date(paste0(year, "-07-01"))),
      "years"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-first_year)

### Account for Capitalized City Names
df <- df %>%
  mutate(city = str_to_title(city)) %>%
  mutate(agency = str_to_title(agency)) %>%
  mutate(city = as.factor(city)) %>%
  mutate(agency = as.factor(agency))

### Remove Zipcode Extension
df <- df %>%
  mutate(zip = as.character(zip), zip = substr(zip, 1, 5))

### Add name
df <- df %>%
  mutate(name = paste(first_name, last_name))

saveRDS(df, file.path(
  dirname(this.path()),
  "..",
  "data",
  "clean",
  "annual_salary_data.rds"
))

Adjust for Inflaiton

Account for inflation using the consumer price index with 2024 as the base year.

CPI Adjustment 
yearly_cpi <- data.frame(
  year = 2010:2024,
  cpi = c(218.1, 224.9, 229.6, 233.0, 236.7, 237.0, 240.0,
          245.1, 251.1, 255.7, 258.8, 271.0, 292.7, 304.7,
          313.7)
) 

df <- df %>%
  left_join(yearly_cpi, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(adj_annual_rate = gross_pay * (313.7 / cpi)) %>%
  select(-cpi)

rows_to_drop <- df %>%
  filter(year > 2024) %>%
  nrow()
df <- df %>%
  filter(year <= 2024)
print(paste("Dropped rows", rows_to_drop, "with a year after 2024."))
[1] "Dropped rows 114729 with a year after 2024."

Adding Gender

Used IQR for Hire Date to Judge Name Window

Code 
summary(df$hire_date)
        Min.      1st Qu.       Median         Mean      3rd Qu.         Max. 
"1954-12-16" "1996-11-18" "2006-01-20" "2004-04-30" "2012-11-02" "2024-06-13"

Note the package could only go as recent as 2012.

Use Gender Package 
names <- df %>%
  distinct(first_name) %>%
  pull(first_name)

gender_output <- gender(names, method = "ssa", years = c(1998, 2012))

gender_by_name <- gender_output %>%
  # filter(proportion_male < .4 | proportion_male > .6) %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice_max(year_max, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%  
  ungroup() %>%
  select(name, gender)

df <- df %>%
  left_join(gender_by_name, by = c("first_name" = "name"))

rows_to_remove <- df %>% 
  filter(is.na(gender)) %>%
  nrow()
df <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(gender))
print(paste("Removed", rows_to_remove, "rows where gender could not be determined."))
[1] "Removed 58085 rows where gender could not be determined."

Goal

  • Are there groups that had atypical wage changes around 2020?

Add Percent Change

Calculate Percent Change 
df <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(adj_annual_rate))

df <- df %>%
  arrange(employee_id, year) %>%
  group_by(employee_id) %>%
  mutate(adj_annual_rate_pct_change = 
           if_else(
             !is.na(lag(adj_annual_rate)) & lag(adj_annual_rate) != 0,
             (adj_annual_rate - lag(adj_annual_rate)) / lag(adj_annual_rate) * 100,
             NA_real_
           )) %>%
  ungroup()

breaks  <- c(-100, -10, 0, 10, 100, Inf)
labels  <- c("- 100%-10%", "- 10%-0%", "0%-10%", "10%-100%", "100%+")

df <- df %>%
  mutate(adj_annual_rate_pct_change_bin = cut(
    adj_annual_rate_pct_change, 
    breaks = breaks, 
    labels = labels, 
    include.lowest = TRUE, 
    right = FALSE
  ))

df <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(adj_annual_rate_pct_change))
Code 
df %>%
  filter(year >= 2016) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = adj_annual_rate_pct_change_bin, fill = gender)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~year) +
  labs(
    x = "Annual Pay % Change (binned)", 
    y = "Count",
    title = "Percent Change in Adjusted Annual Pay by Gender and Fiscal Year",
    fill = "Gender"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

Filter for Top Agencies

df_filtered <- df %>%

Filter for Top Jobs

Code 
top_jobs <- df %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  count(job, name = "Count") %>%
  arrange(desc(Count)) %>%
  filter(Count >= 500) %>%
  pull(job)

df_filtered <- df_filtered %>%
  filter(job %in% top_jobs)

Basic Linear Model

Code 
result <- lm(
  adj_annual_rate_pct_change ~ 
  gender + 
  job + 
  agency + 
  years_since_hired, 
  data = df_filtered %>% 
    filter(year == 2020)
  )
tidy(result) %>%
  filter(p.value < .05) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header("Basic Regression Checking for Factors")

Checking for Multiplicative Relationships

Code 
result <- lm(
  adj_annual_rate_pct_change ~ 
  gender *
  job *
  agency *
  years_since_hired, 
  data = df_filtered %>% 
    filter(year == 2020)
  )
tidy(result) %>%
  filter(p.value < .05) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Multiplicative Regression Checking for Factors"
  )

Conclusions

Regression led to investigation of Judicial Employees which didn’t show the effect anticipated. A hunch that Transportation wages would be negatively affected durring Covid years did result in some preliminary findings that support that idea.
